rounds.hypothesis: check_single_mapping=true is the whole defect, so flipping it to false on both the shrink and expand path is enough: the shrink path already truncates across fragments via alloc_free_region_exact_truncate, and the expand path only needs the relaxed precondition.
rounds.change: Split modify_heap_end into a shrink branch and an expand branch, both calling vmar.resize_mapping(..., false).
rounds.outcome: Rejected on reading VmarInner::resize_mapping rather than on a boot. Its expand path (vmar_impls/mod.rs:472-474) does find_one(&(old_map_end - 1)) then debug_assert_eq!(last_mapping.map_end(), old_map_end) and unconditionally enlarges whatever mapping it finds. Under brk02 that mapping is the PROT_READ page created by mprotect, so the relaxed flag would have grown the read-only VMA instead of adding a writable one - the new heap page would fault on write, violating the invariant's 'newly exposed heap pages must have the default heap permissions' clause even if the syscall returned the right break. It also panics on a debug build when the heap top was munmap'd and no mapping ends at old_map_end.

rounds.hypothesis: Expansion is not a resize of an existing mapping at all. Linux's do_brk_flags treats it as a fresh VM_DATA_DEFAULT_FLAGS region that merges with the predecessor only when flags match, so the heap layer should create a new RW mapping over [old_heap_end, new_heap_end) and let the VMAR's own merge logic coalesce it when permissions happen to agree.
rounds.change: Kept resize_mapping(..., false) for the shrink branch, and replaced the expand branch with vmar.new_map(expansion_size, READ|WRITE).offset(VmarMapOffset::FixedNoReplace(old_heap_end)).build().
rounds.outcome: green: 'brk02: pass', Passed: 2 / Failed: 0, and 'All conformance tests passed.' Both the libc and raw-syscall variants pass, so the post-mprotect expand and the shrink-back step that the test never previously reached both work.

layer: Process heap-management layer (Heap::modify_heap_end in kernel/src/process/process_vm/heap.rs), matching diagnose.json's owning_layer. The invariant is brk-specific - 'the program break is adjustable regardless of how the heap is partitioned, and new heap pages get default heap permissions' - and only this layer knows the heap's default permissions. VmarInner::resize_mapping is deliberately left alone: it is a generic primitive whose 'enlarge the mapping that ends here' contract is what mremap(MREMAP_FIXED) wants, and weakening it there would have changed mremap semantics to fix brk.
generalizes: The fix is expressed entirely in terms of the heap's own range and the heap's own default permissions; it never inspects the count, permissions, or shape of the mappings inside the heap, so there is no branch on the flag, size, or errno brk02 supplies. Any fragmentation source is covered, not just mprotect: mmap(MAP_FIXED) and munmap inside the heap range reach the same code, and the munmap case (no mapping ends at old_heap_end) is handled by construction rather than by a special case, where the round-1 approach would have panicked. Permission correctness now holds in a case the old code could not even express: expanding a heap whose top page is read-only yields a writable new page, because the permissions come from the heap layer instead of being inherited from whatever VMA happened to sit at the boundary. The expand path keeps both properties the old call provided - build() enforces the RLIMIT_AS check (vmar_impls/map.rs:291-302) and FixedNoReplace routes through alloc_free_region_exact, which fails instead of clobbering an existing mapping, so a blocked expansion still returns Err(current_heap_end) and thus ENOMEM - and it ends in insert_try_merge (map.rs:399), so the ordinary unfragmented heap still coalesces into one VMA and does not accumulate one per brk call. Verified beyond the target: brk01 (grows the break repeatedly and writes to every newly exposed page) passes, as do sbrk01, sbrk02, mprotect02/03/05 and mremap01/02/03/05, confirming the untouched mremap path and the mprotect splitting behavior are unregressed. Other callers: modify_heap_end is reached only from sys_brk, and mremap.rs's resize_mapping(..., true) is intentionally unchanged.
fix_summary: Replaces the single resize_mapping(..., check_single_mapping=true) call in Heap::modify_heap_end with two branches designed against Asterinas's own VMAR abstractions. Shrinking calls resize_mapping(..., false), whose shrink path already delegates to alloc_free_region_exact_truncate and therefore truncates every intersecting VmMapping - a fragmented heap needed nothing more than the relaxed precondition. Expanding stops treating the growth as a resize of an existing VmMapping and instead builds a fresh mapping over [old_heap_end, new_heap_end) through VmarMapOptions with VmPerms::READ | VmPerms::WRITE and VmarMapOffset::FixedNoReplace. VmarMapOptions is the abstraction chosen because it is where Asterinas already centralizes the rlimit check, exact-region allocation, and neighbor merging, so the heap layer states the heap's intent (this range, these default permissions, do not replace anything) and the VMAR layer decides whether that becomes a new VMA or a merge with the predecessor. That mirrors do_brk_flags' vma_merge_new_range-then-fall-back-to-fresh-VMA structure without transplanting Linux's VMA surgery, and it keeps the generic resize_mapping primitive intact for mremap.
